conventions:
LABELLING CONVENTIONS (applied strictly to every document)
- doctype: invoice (incl. credit notes), receipt (till receipt, payment confirmation, paid receipt/Quittung), bank_statement (account statement, bank export), contract (agreement, Vertrag, NDA, lease), letter (formal correspondence that is none of the others), quote (offer/Angebot/quotation/proforma), reminder (payment reminder, dunning, Mahnung, final notice), payslip, tax_document (tax assessment, tax return, VAT return, Steuerbescheid), other (everything else, incl. notes, meeting minutes, order confirmations, delivery notes, newsletters, ledgers, recipes, code, identity documents).
- doc_date: the date the document was issued/written, ISO "YYYY-MM-DD". Statements: the statement date, else the period end. Contracts: the date printed as the date of the agreement (signature/"dated") else the effective date. Payslip: "YYYY-MM" (the pay period month) unless an exact issue date is printed. Letters: the letter date. Receipts: the purchase date. Never a due date, delivery/service date, validity date, birth date, or ID expiry. null when the document has no issue date. For e-mails see below.
- amount: a float with a dot decimal, the amount that identifies the document's value: invoice = the gross total of the invoice (negative for credit notes); receipt = the total paid; quote = the gross total offered; reminder = the total the sender demands now (a "total claim / Gesamtforderung / total due" line including fees if present, else the open invoice amount); payslip = the net payout (Auszahlungsbetrag / net pay); tax_document = the amount to pay or refund if one is printed (positive number), else null; contract = null unless one single contract value is explicitly labelled; letter, bank_statement, other = null. Keep the sign as printed.
- currency: ISO code (EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, JPY, SEK) of that amount, null when amount is null.
- counterparty: the issuing/sending party exactly as printed in the letterhead / sender block / From display name (keep the legal-form suffix: "Beispiel Handels GmbH"); for a person sender, the person's name; null if no sender is identifiable (e.g. a bare till slip with no shop name, or a note).
- reference: the document's own number as printed (invoice no., order/reference no., contract no., quote no.); null if none. ALWAYS null for payslip, tax_document, identity-like documents and other. Never an IBAN, a card number, a tax ID, a personal ID.
- lang: "en" or "de" (the main language).
- Expected for e-mails: doc_date = the date of the Date header (ISO), counterparty = the From display name (without the address), doctype by what the mail IS (an invoice mail whose body carries the invoice data is an invoice; a payment-reminder mail is a reminder; a newsletter/chat/meeting mail is other), amount/reference from the body when present.

ANNOTATION DECISIONS (additions and points the convention text leaves open; evaluators should be aware of them)
1. Reference means the document's OWN printed number, nothing else. A reminder that prints its own number (Mahnung-Nr., Reminder no.) is labelled with that number; a reminder that only cites the dunned invoice number(s) (the final notice 'AR/Final_notice_INV-4410.pdf' and the overdue statement 'reminders/overdue_statement_Oct2025.pdf') is labelled reference null. Likewise a letter that merely cites an invoice number is labelled null unless the letter prints its own "Unser Zeichen" / "Our ref" / "Aktenzeichen".
2. bank_statement reference: only an explicitly labelled statement number is used (Kontoauszug Nr. 3/2025 -> "3/2025"; Statement No 2025/03/0112 -> "2025/03/0112"); null in all other statements. IBANs and account numbers are never references.
3. bank_statement doc_date: statement date, else period end. A bare CSV export that prints neither (downloads/transactions.csv) has doc_date null even though it contains booking dates.
4. Identity-like documents (passport data page, residence-permit card): doctype other and EVERY other field null, including lang (null), even though the pages are bilingual. lang is therefore null for exactly these two documents.
5. Order confirmations and delivery notes are doctype other: amount null and reference null (as for all 'other'), but doc_date and counterparty are kept when printed.
6. Contracts: counterparty is the letterhead party; a contract without letterhead (Freelance/Consulting_Agreement_Alex_Example.pdf) uses the first-named party. Amount is set only where a single contract value is explicitly labelled (Total License Fee USD 36,000.00; Vertragswert EUR 16,200.00); monthly rents, salaries and rate cards stay null.
7. Tax documents: counterparty is the issuing authority when an authority issued the document (assessment, acknowledgement, notice); for returns prepared by the taxpayer (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung, VAT return summary) it is the taxpayer printed in the heading. amount = the balance to pay or the refund, as a positive number (refunds carry no minus sign in the text).
8. Payslip doc_date is "YYYY-MM"; the one payslip that prints "Abrechnung erstellt am" has a full ISO date. Payslips print no pay date.
9. Pro forma invoices are quotes (not invoices). Credit notes are invoices with a negative amount, taken with the sign printed.
10. Hotel / travel receipts: doc_date is the receipt date, not arrival or departure.
11. A gift voucher with only a validity date is doctype other with doc_date null.
12. A bare till slip with no shop name has counterparty null and reference null.
13. A formal e-mail that is one-to-one correspondence (cancellation confirmation) is a letter; newsletters, shipping notices, meeting invitations, chat-like mails and account-welcome mails are other (addition to the e-mail rule above).
14. A payment-confirmation reference is the printed receipt/document number (Belegnummer, Receipt number), not the transaction's order number.
15. Counterparty keeps the printed capitalisation (e.g. "FOO WIDGETS INC" when the letterhead is upper case, "Foo Widgets Inc" when it is mixed case); a comparison may normalise case, the labels do not.
16. E-mail doc_date is the calendar date shown in the Date header in the header's own UTC offset (no conversion to UTC); no mail is timed near midnight.
17. Several documents carry OCR-style noise (swapped l/1 and O/0, missing umlauts, joined words). The noise never touches the tokens of counterparty, reference, amount or date; labels are the clean printed values.
18. Documents that contain exactly one date-like string: the Kassenbon whose only date is "14.03.25 17:42", the till slips and receipts, letters and one consulting agreement whose only date is written with a month name (March 14, 2025 / 14-Mar-2025 / 14. März 2025 / 2 June 2025 / 14 October 2025 / 04 Nov 2024), and the coffee receipt with 14/03/2025. A second two-digit-year document (a scanned invoice from 2023) carries three such dates.
19. Dates earlier than the document date (invoice date, order date) and later dates (due, validity, contract end, ID expiry) appear inside many documents as distractors; they are never the label.

5. WORKSTREAM NARRATIVES
Platform and hosting. The production, test and staging environments were handed over by the hosting provider on schedule. Network segmentation, backup policies and monitoring dashboards are in place. Capacity tests showed headroom of roughly thirty percent over the planned peak load. The remaining items are the disaster recovery exercise and the final tuning of alert thresholds.

Data migration. Two rehearsals of the customer master load were completed. The first rehearsal exposed duplicate records caused by inconsistent spelling of company names. A matching rule set was agreed with the business and reduced duplicates by about eighty percent. The remaining duplicates need manual review by the sales operations team, which is the main driver of the delay.

Application migration. Wave one covered the intranet, the document store, the ticketing tool and the time recording tool. All four moved at weekends with less than two hours of downtime. User feedback has been positive. Wave two covers the finance applications and depends on the year-end close calendar.

Integration. The interface catalogue lists thirty-two interfaces, of which twenty-six have passed end-to-end tests. The remaining six relate to the legacy reporting server and will be rebuilt once the reporting component licence has been resolved.

Security and access. Role definitions were reviewed with the data owners. Single sign-on is working for all migrated applications. A penetration test by an independent provider is scheduled for the first half of the next quarter.

Training and change. Forty super-users have been identified, but only twenty-two have attended the first session. The change team will offer evening slots and short video guides to close the gap before wave two.

# Paperwork notes

Last updated: 2025-04-10

A short reminder to myself about how the small office handles documents.
